analysis:
This PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one passthrough-table row at head line 1687 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, and docs/provider/direct-mode.md describes load-time shape warmup during standalone preload. The only changed lines in the supplied cli-reference.md units are that row (head 1687); the rest of the head text is unchanged context, which I skimmed for consistency but did not audit. No code or control changes are visible here.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new variable is listed in the table of variables that `darkbloom start` copies into the LaunchAgent plist. The documented effects are only `0` (disable the warmup) and `always` (skip the shader-cache probe). These are performance and timing knobs that neither relax encryption, attestation or authorization nor touch the prefix cache or the TB-011 serving authorization. No threat-model asset or boundary is affected on the documented evidence.
- The docs say warmup runs before the listener opens in direct mode, and that the 5-second sweep tick warms a deferred engine once the server is idle, with a request preempting it. If the implementation uses synthetic or fixed shapes, it adds no consumer data. The docs do not say what prompts or shapes it uses. Whether warmup touches the prefix cache (T-041/SEC-035) or leaves residual GPU state (T-028) is not stated and cannot be verified from the supplied docs.
- The variable is placed in the daemon passthrough list alongside other tuning variables. A local operator controls the environment anyway (ADV-001 is already in scope), so this adds no new privilege.

Open integration question: the implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and the sweep-tick warmup path is not supplied, so I can't confirm the documented behavior or that warmup requests cannot populate or probe the SSD prefix cache or run during the coordinator-serving admission window. No findings.
